confidence_notes: The food and drink anchors use a small number of web searches. Coffee and the inexpensive meal are reasonably well supported by crowd-sourced Wollongong data from MyLifeElsewhere, which put a cappuccino near AUD 5.6 and a basic meal near AUD 23–25. The beer anchor is also based on that data, but its sources disagreed, with a pint at about AUD 8.6–9.1 depending on the source. I raised it slightly to about AUD 10 for mid-2026 inflation, so treat it as moderately uncertain. The mid-range meal for two is based on a Numbeo-derived figure of about AUD 123, dated June 2026 and seen through a mirror site. Its reported range was wide, about AUD 90–184. The cocktail and wine anchors are weaker. The only aggregate cocktail figure I found was AUD 16 for a downtown club, based on just 7 data points. The other drink prices I found were undated happy-hour deals, including cocktails at AUD 10–13 and wine at AUD 10. I estimated regular menu prices of about AUD 20 for a cocktail and AUD 12–13 for a glass of wine, using these signals and the usual Australian price relationship to beer. The four accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates only. I did not search booking sites or check listings. Wollongong has very few registered hostels, so the hostel dorm and private-room anchors are the least certain. July is winter low season, which keeps the hotel and motel estimates moderate.
comparable_city_reasoning: Wollongong is a regional coastal city in New South Wales about 80 km south of Sydney. Its restaurant and drink prices are a little below or close to the Australian average, and are cheaper than central Sydney. Its prices are broadly similar to Newcastle NSW and Geelong VIC. Accommodation was estimated against regional NSW coastal cities, using winter-season rates for basic motels and 3-star hotels.
